problem.name_latex: Maximum independent set in unit-disk graphs
problem.name: Maximum independent set in unit-disk graphs
problem.statement_latex:
Given points $r_1,\ldots,r_n\in\mathbb R^2$ and a blockade radius $R$, let $\{i,j\}\in E$ when $\|r_i-r_j\|\le R$. Find the largest $S\subseteq[n]$ with $\|r_i-r_j\|>R$ for distinct $i,j\in S$. This geometric promise makes independent-set constraints directly implementable with atom interactions.
The experiment measures analog evolution time and repetitions to success; the exact classical comparison uses time on explicitly represented geometric graphs.

quantum.headline_latex: $t\lceil\log\delta/\log(1-p)\rceil$ evolution time to success probability $1-\delta$, Rydberg adiabatic and variational optimization.
quantum.details_latex: Here $p$ is the measured single-run success probability and $t$ the evolution duration. State preparation, readout and parameter tuning add to the total time. Experiments with up to 289 atoms reported favorable scaling against an optimized simulated-annealing comparator on the tested graph families.

classical.headline_latex: $2^{O(\sqrt n)}\operatorname{poly}(n)$ for exact unit-disk independent set, geometric separators and dynamic programming.
classical.details_latex: The geometric promise is essential: weighted separators and tree decompositions for similarly sized fat objects yield the subexponential exact algorithm in the plane. A polynomial-time approximation scheme is available for unit-disk graphs at fixed approximation error. Simulated annealing is the experimental comparator, while the geometric separator algorithm supplies the exact worst-case comparison.
